name: Anisotropic Random Fourier Features Mapping
definition: A feature mapping scheme that employs multiple bandwidths to model multidimensional signal characteristics, addressing the heterogeneity of plenoptic functions across different dimensions (spatial vs. angular) which isotropic methods fail to handle.
summary: Anisotropic Random Fourier Features Mapping uses per-dimension bandwidths to model heterogeneous signal frequencies, avoiding the imbalanced regression and detail loss of isotropic methods.
